title: Staff run stock and fulfilment from one console
problem_statement: Merchant staff have no single place to keep stock honest and move paid orders to the customer. Stock drift and fulfilment lag are handled by memory and message threads.
business_value: Staff keep inventory accurate and move paid orders through packing and dispatch from one console, which is the operational handling time and same-day fulfilment KPI in gap-closed 3.3.
why_now: Without it the storefront's stock numbers drift from the shelf within days of launch.

success_criteria.metric: orders whose status an admin advances on the day the customer paid
success_criteria.target: measured from launch as the operational baseline
success_criteria.measurement_method: status-change timestamps in the audit trail (gap-closed 3.3)

success_criteria.metric: stock adjustments recorded without an actor and a reason

decoupling.rationale: Keeping stock accurate and auditable is value staff receive whether or not a single order exists, and it carries its own operational KPI. The fulfilment half does consume orders the purchase epic produces, but that is a sequencing dependency inside a delivery plan, not the business dependency test 3 asks about: this epic's value proposition does not require the other to have shipped.
merged_from: candidate EPIC-INVENTORY admin half - the same console, the same operational value (test 3)
candidate EPIC-ORDER admin-fulfilment half - the same console, the same operational value (test 3)

in: stock adjustment with a mandatory reason
the paid to packing to shipped to delivered progression
an audit record on every change
out_deferred: catalogue and coupon administration - present in the source requirement but outside this sample's scope

tier_signals: back-office actor acting on orders that carry direct personal data (gap-closed 15)
